background: Morgan Stanley is the holding company of a leading US investment bank whose earnings have shifted toward wealth and investment management alongside institutional securities, with a deposit franchise built on brokerage sweeps.
synthesis: Ratings are A on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A-, all three on a stable outlook, with the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of them on 4 Nov 2022. Risk-based capital is strong — CET1 of 14.9% is in the top quarter of US banks — but leverage of 4.9% is in the bottom quarter, the usual consequence of a large securities balance sheet. Liquidity is strong, LCR of 129% in the top quarter, and the only real movement is leverage, down 0.6 points since 30 Jun 2025 (figures to 30 Jun 2026). Flagged items are conduct and controls rather than credit: the newest, on 24 Sep 2026, a client email that disclosed a deal pipeline, alongside an earlier litigation matter.
